summary: US-008 (SPIKE): Pressure-test the generalized dated-slot model
description:
**As** the team, **I want** to prove the ADR-005 slot abstraction survives the hard cases **before** US-009 (TKT-51) hardens the schema, so a bad generic design doesn't hurt every downstream vertical.

**Priority:** P0
**Type:** Spike (timeboxed, no production code — analysis + ADR amendment only)
**Depends on:** —

`risk:low` — investigation only, produces docs/an ADR, touches no service code or migration; the schema decision it produces is what US-009 implements under the full plan gate. (Challengeable: if the spike ends up needing throwaway prototype code in a service, drop the label.)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A written analysis (in `docs/` + an ADR-005 amendment) models three stress cases against a candidate slot shape: **re-entry** (a park pass holder exits and re-enters the same operating day — multi-entry vs the single-redemption performance case), **mid-day capacity change** (an operating day's capacity is raised/cut while entries are live — where the number-of-authority lives, catalog vs inventory, and behaviour when cut below current occupancy), and **weather closure** (an operating day closes partway through — slot state, effect on already-admitted vs not-yet-arrived holders, refund signalling)
- [ ] For each case the analysis names **which attributes live on the catalog slot** vs **what the inventory claim core owns** (the ADR-005 boundary), and produces the concrete attribute set + state machine US-009 will implement (slot kind, operating hours, re-entry policy, closure)
- [ ] Verdict: the unified model holds (with the documented attribute shape) **or** a scoped exception is recorded as a new ADR — either outcome unblocks US-009 with a decided schema

Quality gate (spike): the output is a reviewed decision doc/ADR, not code; no `make check` surface. Exit is the recorded verdict.

binding.rule: Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; lodging/day resources reserve through the same contention-safe core; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

Append-only trails, one discipline: money journal is immutable/hash-chained/signed and ticket/entitlement state changes are append-only lifecycle events; trails are pseudonymous (no raw PII in any append-only record); NF525 is a later-phase profile that must layer on without schema or flow changes.

reference.summary: PRD v1 — TKT-2 catalog & event structure user stories (US-007…US-011)
ADR-005 unified dated-slot admission — the load-bearing abstraction this epic hardens; §Consequences names re-entry/mid-day-capacity/weather-closure as the pressure tests
